arguments.premise_synthesis: Gold's price movements have historically preceded major monetary policy shifts and sovereign debt crises. In June/July 2019, gold broke out before the repo market crisis and subsequent quantitative easing in 2020. It topped in August 2020 before inflation appeared. After a sideways period during the tightening cycle from 2020 to 2024, gold broke out again in March 2024 anticipating future interest rate cuts and QE, and continued rising into 2025 as the odds of a Fed rate cut exceeded 90%. Central banks are among the largest buyers, reinforcing gold's role as a monetary indicator. The price has reached $3,500 per ounce, 1,000 times its 1971 level, reflecting long-term monetary debasement and the erosion of the dollar system.
arguments.conclusion_supported: The evidence establishes that gold's price surges consistently act as a leading indicator of monetary policy easing and sovereign debt crises, supporting the central claim.
